about: Home's lines of the day, one a day by the date. Each is in English, by a writer dead more than seventy years, so it has no translator and no rights to clear; an observation, never an instruction, and nothing about the body or money. Each was read word for word in a public-domain text of its work, a whole sentence or whole lines of verse, in that text's own spelling and punctuation.

lines.text: Time is but the stream I go a-fishing in.
The years teach much which the days never know.
Well done is better than well said.
Things won are done; joy's soul lies in the doing.
What is now proved was once only imagined.
lines.from: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, 1790

lines.text: Our life is frittered away by detail.
Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
There is no charm equal to tenderness of heart.
There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact.
It's a poor sort of memory that only works backwards.
To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.
Experience is the name every one gives to their mistakes.
Work is love made visible.
An adventure is only an inconvenience rightly considered.
Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me.
The reward of a thing well done, is to have done it.
Lost time is never found again.
The readiness is all.
No bird soars too high if he soars with his own wings.
lines.from: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, 1790

lines.text: Few things are impossible to diligence and skill.
It is not down in any map; true places never are.
Few things are harder to put up with than the annoyance of a good example.
Reading maketh a full man; conference a ready man; and writing an exact man.
Things do not change; we change.
The only reward of virtue is virtue; the only way to have a friend is to be one.
There is more day to dawn. The sun is but a morning star.
Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
One half of the world cannot understand the pleasures of the other.
It is a capital mistake to theorize before one has data.
Little strokes fell great oaks.
Our doubts are traitors / And make us lose the good we oft might win / By fearing to attempt.
The busy bee has no time for sorrow.
lines.from: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, 1790

lines.text: Heaven is under our feet as well as over our heads.
The invariable mark of wisdom is to see the miraculous in the common.
A lake is the landscape's most beautiful and expressive feature.
Nature always wears the colors of the spirit.
Why, sometimes I've believed as many as six impossible things before breakfast.
'Tis better to have loved and lost / Than never to have loved at all.
The truth is rarely pure and never simple.
Your joy is your sorrow unmasked.
Angels can fly because they can take themselves lightly.
Vision is the art of seeing things invisible.
What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult to each other?
If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?
Hope is the thing with feathers / That perches in the soul
I am large, I contain multitudes.
Life appears to me too short to be spent in nursing animosity, or registering wrongs.
Where you tend a rose, my lad, / A thistle cannot grow.
Ah, but a man's reach should exceed his grasp, / Or what's a Heaven for?
Variety's the very spice of life, / That gives it all its flavour.
It is impossible to enjoy idling thoroughly unless one has plenty of work to do.
lines.from: Idle Thoughts of an Idle Fellow, 1886

lines.text: Isn't it splendid to think of all the things there are to find out about?
I never found the companion that was so companionable as solitude.
Nothing is at last sacred but the integrity of your own mind.
Diligence is the mother of good luck.
How far that little candle throws his beams! / So shines a good deed in a naughty world.
Energy is Eternal Delight.
lines.from: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, 1790

lines.text: We have all a better guide in ourselves, if we would attend to it, than any other person can be.
You see, but you do not observe.
I had three chairs in my house; one for solitude, two for friendship, three for society.
People wish to be settled; only as far as they are unsettled is there any hope for them.
The morning wind forever blows, the poem of creation is uninterrupted; but few are the ears that hear it.
We live amid surfaces, and the true art of life is to skate well on them.
He that can have patience can have what he will.
We are such stuff / As dreams are made on, and our little life / Is rounded with a sleep.
Exuberance is Beauty.
lines.from: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, 1790

lines.text: Example is always more efficacious than precept.
I know not all that may be coming, but be it what it will, I'll go to it laughing.
Nothing so needs reforming as other people's habits.
Prosperity is not without many fears and distastes; and adversity is not without comforts and hopes.
I love a broad margin to my life.
A friend is a person with whom I may be sincere.
Now, here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place.
For men may come and men may go, / But I go on for ever.
I can resist everything except temptation.
Your friend is your needs answered.
The world will never starve for want of wonders; but only for want of wonder.
Till this moment, I never knew myself.
It has long been an axiom of mine that the little things are infinitely the most important.
The universe is wider than our views of it.
Though we travel the world over to find the beautiful, we must carry it with us, or we find it not.
The used key is always bright.
The fool doth think he is wise, but the wise man knows himself to be a fool.
Eternity is in love with the productions of time.
lines.from: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, 1790

lines.text: It is never too late to give up our prejudices.
In the woods, we return to reason and faith.
